name: Bell Fritters
description: Historical recipe from The Virginia Housewife; Or, Methodical Cook (1824). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Put a piece of butter the size of an egg into a pint of water
let it boil a few minutes
thicken it very smoothly with a pint of flour
let it remain a short time on the fire, stir it all the time that it may not stick to the pan
pour it in a wooden bowl
add five or six eggs, breaking one and beating it in--then another, and so on till they are all in, and the dough quite light
put a pint of lard in a pan, let it boil
make the fritters small, and fry them of a fine amber colour

source.author: Mary Randolph
source.originalInstructions:
1. Put a piece of butter the size of an egg into a pint of water
2. let it boil a few minutes
3. thicken it very smoothly with a pint of flour
4. let it remain a short time on the fire, stir it all the time that it may not stick to the pan
5. pour it in a wooden bowl
6. add five or six eggs, breaking one and beating it in--then another, and so on till they are all in, and the dough quite light
7. put a pint of lard in a pan, let it boil
8. make the fritters small, and fry them of a fine amber colour
